reason: The passage consistently depicts Yahweh as intimately associated with Israel as a collective national entity. The entire narrative centers on Yahweh's direct guidance of 'all the congregation of the children of Israel' (כָּל־ עֲדַת בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל), their journeys ordered 'according to the word/mouth of Yahweh' (עַל־ פִּי יְהוָה), and Yahweh's miraculous intervention to meet the nation's material needs. The climactic question—'Is Yahweh in our midst or not?' (הֲיֵשׁ יְהוָה בְקִרְבֵּנוּ אִם־ אָיִן)—positions Yahweh as the God whose presence defines the collective identity and welfare of Israel. This portrayal is characteristic of a national God: a deity whose primary agency and concern are bound to a specific people's survival, sustenance, and identity.
